newsitem.title: USA: Iraq to submit new oil price formula by Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Iraq to submit new oil price formula by Wednesday.

text.p: Iraq submitted a new oil price formula for approval by the United Nations' "oil-for-food" deal overseers, but oil traders said the prices were "too aggressive" and a new formula is expected by Wednesday, according to sources.

Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) submitted a price for U.S. buyers of its Basrah Light crude of $4.40 under regional benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI), or 20 cents above the $4.60 discount applying in May when its oil was last lifted.
Iraq moved the U.S. price up in line with the changes since May in Saudi Arabia's Light crude but traders said freight rates meanwhile have become more expensive.
"We can't sell it at those numbers. Since the last time Iraqi oil was lifted the freight costs have gone up 60 cents per barrel.
Nevertheless, diplomats said they do not see any serious obstacle to the price formula getting approved and oil exports being resumed under the "oil-for-food" deal.
"Iraq and the U.N. overseers had an exchange of views and the Iraqis agreed to come back later today or early Wednesday with a fax," said a senior Wetern diplomat.
"I wouldn't view it as a hitch though," he said. "Once they transmit the fax it will go through very quickly."
The oil price formula, once agreed by the U.N. overseers, is then passed to the U.N. Sanctions Committee which automatically approves after 48 hours unless an objection is raised.
